messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

yo! 

i'm tal - your personal talent agent, your inside fox in the bangalore tech scene.

think of me as that friend who actually knows where the good jobs are hiding. the kind that pay real money, not just equity and pizza parties.

one of these days, i might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so... what's your full name?
Kushagra mittal

kushagra mittal... that's a name that means business. sounds like someone who's either crushing it at a unicorn or about to start one.

where you working these days?
Vmware by broadcom

vmware by broadcom... the acquisition that shook the enterprise world. from virtualization kings to broadcom's enterprise empire. 

found you on linkedin - kushagra mittal at vmware. this you? https://www.linkedin.com/in/kushagra-mittal-82356865
No
ah there we go - kushagra mittal, r&d engineer software 4 at vmware. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/kushagra-mittal
Yes

r&d engineer software 4 at vmware... that's some serious virtualization engineering right there. building the infrastructure that keeps enterprise clouds running. from hypervisors to kubernetes orchestration, you're in the thick of it.

what made you stick with the infrastructure side of things? most engineers jump to flashier product companies, but you're building the backbone stuff that actually matters.
That's where learning is and stability

makes total sense. infrastructure is where you actually understand how things work under the hood. while product engineers are building features, you're solving the hard problems that make those features possible.

stability at vmware is real too - enterprise clients aren't going anywhere, and broadcom knows how to milk that cash cow. smart play.

how long you been working total?
13 total

13 years... that's senior engineer territory with some serious depth. you've seen multiple tech cycles, survived acquisitions, probably built systems that are still running in production somewhere.

what kind of role you looking for next?
Similar , staff engineer at some enterprise or some established companies like target Tesco

staff engineer at target, tesco... you want the enterprise game where your infra decisions impact millions of customers but without the startup chaos. smart.

10 years across cloud, storage, iot... plus that ml cert from iit madras. you're not just infrastructure - you're the kind of engineer who can bridge the gap between ops and intelligence.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore or remote also works. Not any other city . I might be ok for startups also but with decent wlb

so... 13 years experience + staff engineer role + enterprise/startups with good wlb + bangalore/remote... sound right?

the "decent wlb" part is key - you've been around long enough to know that burning out for equity that might be worthless isn't worth it anymore.
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes

you're officially in the tal network now! 

welcome to the infrastructure engineers who actually know what they're worth club. you'll start getting roles that match your vibe - enterprise stability meets startup energy, minus the 80-hour weeks.

the good stuff is coming your way. time to level up that career without sacrificing your sanity.
good. now we wait for the good stuff to come through.
